description:
FILED s483b (Opus, 2026-09-13) from the #1619 probe battery.  PRE-EXISTING on
main e3767cff (probed there and on the s483b tree; unchanged by #1619's fix).

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    package H; sub who { "H::who" }
    package main;
    my $h = bless {}, 'H'; my $r = \$h;
    print $$r->who, "\n";
    perl:  H::who
    PCL:   Can't call method who on unblessed reference

CAUSE, LOCATED (read in the emission, not guessed): `$$r->who` is parsed as
`${ $r->who }`, i.e. the method call is taken as the DEREF's operand, where
perl binds the sigil deref tighter than `->`:  ${$r}->who.

    $ printf 'my $h = bless {}, "H"; my $r = \\$h; print $$r->who;\n' | ./pl2cl
    ... (p-print (p-cast-$ (p-list-ctx (p-method-call $r "who"))))

The subscript siblings are RIGHT -- `$$r{k}` and `$$r[0]` parse as
`${$r}{k}` / `${$r}[0]` -- so this is the `->` METHOD arm of the same
postfix-chain decision, not the deref itself.  The value-returning spelling
`${$r}->who` works today.

BAR: ~10 probe shapes vs perl including the ones that must NOT change
(`$$r{k}`, `$$r[0]`, `$$$rr->who`, `@$r`, `$$r` alone, a method name that is
also a sub in scope), a guard row beside the others, inverse-verified.
SIZE: S-M (a PExpr postfix-chain fix; corpus-diff + emission-ab + gen bump).

=== DONE (s483c) ===
CAUSE, exactly: the rule was NOT missing from the compiler â it was in TWO of
the arrow arms PRIVATELY, each with its own cast-run walk (#305 for
`$$r->(â¦)`, #211 for `$$r->{k}` / `$$r->[0]`), and absent from the six
others.  So every METHOD spelling (bareword, `name(args)`, `Pkg::name`,
`$var`, `$var(args)`, computed `${\ "name"}()`), every POSTFIX-DEREF arm
(`->@*`, `->$#*`, `->%*`, `->@[â¦]`) and â through them â the braced
spelling `${$r}->who` read the cast as a deref OF THE METHOD CALL.
**The task's claim that `${$r}->who` works today is WRONG** (measured: it
dies on the base tree like the rest).  12 of 24 probe shapes were wrong, one
SILENTLY: `$$ar->$#*` answered -1, and `$$arr->@*` "Not a SCALAR
reference".

FIX: ONE reading (CLAUDE.md rule 11) â `Pl::PExpr::_arrow_invocant` takes the
run start from `_cast_run_start`, folds it into the invocant only when
`_all_scalar_casts` (a non-`$` cast is not a deref level: `@$r` is already
the array), and returns the splice START with the node; every arrow arm asks
it.  `\` is excluded by `_cast_run_start` because `\` is an OPERATOR and a
lower-precedence one: `\$x->m` is `\($x->m)` (probed â `ref(\$h->self)`
is REF).  `_reduce_pre` gained a 5th argument `$start` so the reduction
consumes the run instead of leaving its casts in the stream; with no run
`$start == $$i-1` and the splice arithmetic is byte-identical to before.
The no-arrow subscript arm is untouched: its reading is different (the
OUTERMOST cast picks the access kind) and correct.

MEASURED
  * 43 probe shapes vs perl 5.40.3 in three batteries (scratch/s483c/probes/
    p1620.pl 19, p1620b.pl 24 = the arms the first battery missed, p1620c.pl
    21 = the would-it-break set).  Every row identical to perl except three
    that are BASE-IDENTICAL â #1628, filed.
  * corpus-diff vs 6eea8578: emission IDENTICAL over 111 files + 6 shapes,
    silent drops 5 unchanged.
  * emission-ab vs 6eea8578 over 1034 files (lib/ 22, cpan-tests/modules 402,
    perl's own t/ 604, shapes 6): SAME=1033 DIFF=1 RCDIFF=0.  The ONE DIFF is
    this bug in real code: Test-Simple-1.302199's Test/Builder.pm
    `_unoverload` (`$$thing->isa('UNIVERSAL')`,
    `$$thing = $$thing->$string_meth(undef, 0)`).  Probed as a program
    (probes/p1620d.pl, three branches): the new emission matches perl in all
    three, the old one DIES "Can't call method can on unblessed reference".
  * gate-set-scan over BOTH populations (638 files) vs the base extraction:
    IDENTICAL â no verdict moved.
  * ir-host-leak identical to base (31 symbols); ir-conform 321 pass / 0 fail
    / 24 known / 0 stale.
  * FULL sweep (perl tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 4): GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, TOTAL passing 18675 = baseline (+0), dropped statements census 5 / current 5 (+0).  The 5 UNSTABLE rows (method.t 2, magic.t 1, yadayada.t 2) are crash-file noise: method.t's fail SET is byte-identical between the base extraction and this tree (23 rows, 76 pass both).
  * FULL gate on the final rebased tree: 236 files / 8097 rows, failures ONLY xs-01/02/03 (the 13 standing pclxs rows) = green.  The base extraction is 235 files / 8091 with the new 70-row raw-verdict-01.t in place, i.e. 8081 + 10 + 6 = 8097 exactly.
  * guard Pl/t/deref-arrow-01.t (6 rows, 0.8 s), INVERSE-verified on a
    6eea8578 `git archive` extraction: rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 FAIL there, row 3 â
    the must-not-change side â passes on both.
Generation v2-1320; the three checked-in artifacts regenerated.
subject: `$$r->who` is parsed as `${ $r->who }` -- perl binds the sigil deref tighter than `->` (the `{k}`/`[0]` siblings are right)
